quests.explanation: Structural remedies (unbundling) are the most severe competition intervention - they break up the company's integrated services. Regulators resort to structural remedies only when behavioural remedies ('do this, don't do that') have failed to restore competition.

quests.explanation: Platform cooperatives transfer ownership from capital to labour - the workers own the algorithm rather than being controlled by it. quests.explanation: A platform cooperative requires a distinct legal form because standard cooperative law was designed before algorithmic platforms existed. Three unique features - worker governance (democratic control of the algorithm), revenue sharing (distributed profits), and algorithmic transparency (workers know how they are evaluated) - distinguish it from traditional cooperatives.
